data.name: Gatiksha
data.gender_notes: Gatiksha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Goddess of the Goals or Steps
data.long_meaning: Gati means 'goals' or 'steps'. Ksha means 'field' or 'space'. Thus, Gatiksha means 'Goddess of the Goals' or 'Goddess of the Steps'. She is believed to guide and protect those who seek to achieve their goals in life. The name Gatiksha carries the meaning “Goddess of the Goals or Steps” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gatiksha usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the goals or steps and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the journey towards personal growth and self-realization.
data.etymology: Gatiksha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Goals or Steps.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gatiksha total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Gautami Putra Satakarni, a Satavahana king of the Andhra region, ruled from around 78 CE to 130 CE. He is also known as Mahasatakarni and Gautamiputra Bhagabhati. In later Hindu tradition, he was revered as the incarnation of the god Vishnu. The name 'Gatiksha' is derived from 'Gautami Putra', meaning 'son of Gautami'.

The Puranas mention a celestial maiden named Gatiksha, who was the mother of the goddess Parvati. In Hindu mythology, Parvati is the wife of Shiva. Gatiksha is also referred to as the 'Mother of Parvati'.
